title: Plus d’une décennie de transformation éducative Plus d’une décennie de transformation éducative : étude de cas de l’Institut des sciences, des technologies et des études avancées d’Haïti (ISTEAH)
abstract: Cet article analyse le rôle de l’Institut des sciences, des technologies et des études avancées d’Haïti (ISTEAH) en matière d’éducation, de démocratie et de soutenabilité dans un contexte national marqué par l’instabilité politique depuis les années 1960. Portée par la diaspora, l’institution représente un modèle alternatif et innovateur de développement. Face aux enjeux de violence, d’inégalité et de ségrégation ainsi qu’aux politiques éducatives et de gouvernance instable, l’ISTEAH produit des connaissances essentielles et cultive l’engagement critique pour soutenir la société haïtienne. Par une analyse de contenus audiovisuels, incluant notamment une entrevue avec le fondateur de l’ISTEAH et des réflexions d’une professeure et d’un étudiant, nous documentons ses apports et ses défis. L’article retrace le cheminement de l’ISTEAH, examine la spécificité de son influence sur Haïti, la diaspora et le monde francophone, et interroge son rôle dans un contexte global marqué par des tensions socio-politiques et des enjeux éducatifs contemporains.

title: Building Capacity for School Crisis Planning: Towards a Professional Development Model for Caribbean Mid-System Education Leaders
abstract: This study examines the experiences of Jamaican education officers (EOs) regarding school crisis plans, specifically what they have learned during their implementation. It also identifies the professional competencies that these officers deem essential for effective crisis preparedness. Employing a qualitative phenomenological approach, the research involved interviews with six EOs and a desk review of Caribbean Disaster Emergency Management Agency’s (CDEMA) Model Safe School Programme. The findings reveal significant discrepancies between written crisis plans and their practical implementation, including limited operational readiness, inadequate adaptability, and unclear governance structures. The results reinforce the necessity for crisis‑specific training in areas such as risk assessment, adaptive leadership, multi‑stakeholder coordination, and instructional continuity. The findings inform a streamlined, competency-based professional development framework for Caribbean mid-system leaders such as EOs to improve crisis resilience within Caribbean educational systems. This study advances comparative education by highlighting the middle-tier as a key unit in crisis planning.

title: Repenser l’innovation éducative par une pédagogie transdisciplinaire des savoirs situés Savoirs situés des enseignants des diasporas africaines et caribéennes en milieu minoritaire
abstract: Cet article propose une perspective transdisciplinaire pour revisiter les défis éducatifs et professionnels rencontrés par les enseignants issus des diasporas africaines et caribéennes en contexte canadien francophone. Elle intègre une analyse conceptuelle nourrie par la pédagogie critique, les épistémologies du Sud, l’éducation comparée, ainsi que des travaux récents sur la reconnaissance des savoirs minorisés et marginalisés. En réponse, nous mobilisons une méthodologie transdisciplinaire centrée sur la reconnaissance des savoirs situés, ancrés dans le perspectivisme et des récits professionnels comme leviers et unités d’analyse et de transformation. Nous argumentons que cette posture permet d’identifier les conditions d’émergence d’une pédagogie inclusive et durable, co-construite entre institutions, enseignants et communautés afin de donner une voix, voire de valider le statut des enseignants africains et caribéens dans le narratif pédagogique canadien francophone. Il propose ainsi une contribution originale aux débats sur le changement systémique en éducation, particulièrement en contexte post migratoire francophone.

title: Considering the Implications of Plurilingual Education in the Anglophone Creole Context of Trinidad and Tobago En tenant compte des implications de l’éducation plurilingue dans le contexte créolophone anglophone de Trinité-et-Tobago
abstract: Trinidad and Tobago is characterized by complex linguistic hierarchies. This study investigates how primary students engage with plurilingual practices in the elementary classroom. Grounded in sociocultural theory (Vygotsky, 1934/1986) and postmodernist epistemology, this study employs an educational design research approach to examine how children navigate classroom interactions shaped by English-Creole diglossia and dominant language ideologies. The study draws on scholarship on Caribbean Englishes (Nero, 2006; Simmons-McDonald, 2004), critical language awareness (Fairclough, 1992, 2013), culturally responsive pedagogy (Ladson-Billings, 2014), and adapted elements from the Language Friendly School framework (Le Pichon-Vorstman & Kambel, 2022) to understand how language-inclusive pedagogy is enacted in context. Findings highlight the central role of teachers as agents of change, and the need for critical Creole language awareness within broader plurilingual education. The study contributes to comparative education by illustrating how global pedagogical movements are reshaped by local sociolinguistic realities of Creole-speaking classrooms, with implications for system-level innova

title: Leadership pédagogique et épistémologies situées en Haïti : entre héritages, ruptures et reconfiguration des savoirs en sciences infirmières. Leadership pédagogique et épistémologies situées en Haïti : entre héritages, ruptures et reconfiguration des savoirs en sciences infirmières
abstract: En Haïti, la formation en sciences infirmières est traversée par des tensions entre modèles curriculaires importés et savoirs locaux marginalisés. Cet article explore comment le leadership pédagogique informel, exercé hors des cadres institutionnels, contribue à une reconfiguration des savoirs en santé, enracinée dans les réalités haïtiennes. En mobilisant les cadres de la justice cognitive et des épistémologies situées, l’étude s’appuie sur une recension documentaire et cinq entretiens exploratoires, inscrits dans un design qualitatif exploratoire. Elle identifie une typologie des tensions épistémiques, des formes d’injustice cognitive et des stratégies pédagogiques de résistance, d’adaptation et d’innovation ascendante. Ces résultats nourrissent le dialogue comparatif sur les transformations éducatives en contexte caribéen et postcolonial.

title: Building Inclusive Education Systems Through UDL: A Caribbean Tripartite Partnership for Teacher Training and Innovation
abstract: This article explores a partnership between a Caribbean NGO, U.S. university, and national governments advancing inclusive education through teacher development. From 2021 to 2024, an institute engaged about 700 educators from the Bahamas, Dominica, Grenada, Jamaica, St. Kitts & Nevis, St. Lucia, and St. Vincent & the Grenadines in a virtual week-long capacity-building program. The institute promotes inclusive learning for neurodiverse classrooms and strategies supporting students with autism, ADHD, and dyslexia. Centred on universal design for learning (UDL), it fosters equitable, evidence-based practice. Two questions guide the paper: (1) How governments, universities, and NGOs collaborate to foster educational innovation, and (2) How educators perceive UDL institutes’ impact on pedagogical content knowledge. Illustrative evidence suggests increased confidence and innovation. We introduce an inclusive practice capacity building model and implications for policymakers, universities, and NGOs. The partnership, locally embedded in the Caribbean, offers insights on teacher preparation, South–North cooperation, and sustainable inclusive reform.

title: Un Partenariats éducatifs et leadership local en contexte d’instabilité chronique Partenariats éducatifs et leadership local en contexte d’instabilité chronique : étude de cas de trois écoles publiques fondamentales à Haïti
abstract: Cet article analyse comment trois écoles publiques en Haïti mobilisent leurs conseils d’école afin de maintenir une continuité éducative dans un contexte d’instabilité. S’appuyant sur une étude qualitative, l’étude examine la manière dont la gouvernance locale se reconfigure lorsque l’appui institutionnel s’affaiblit. Les résultats montrent que les conseils d’école fonctionnent comme des espaces hybrides de gouvernance où se croisent procédures démocratiques, pragmatisme communautaire et leadership distribué. Malgré irrégularités et insécurité persistante, ces conseils démontrent d’importantes capacités d’actions endogènes. Les résultats montrent également que la capacité d’action des conseils d’école demeure fortement dépendante de facteurs contextuels (disponibilité des parents, fragilité institutionnelle, ressources limitées), ce qui limite la portée et la régularité de leur rôle, malgré leur importance dans la gouvernance scolaire. Ces pratiques révèlent des formes de « résilience par le bas » par lesquelles les acteurs réorganisent le fonctionnement scolaire en réponse à la crise.

title: Foreword
Moving From the Periphery to the Centre: Re/Framing Decolonial Educational Innovation in the Caribbean
abstract: This conceptual paper explores the relationship between innovation and decoloniality in education, arguing that educational innovation must go beyond technocratic solutions to challenge the colonial legacies embedded in curricula, teaching methods, and institutional frameworks. Mainstream models of educational reform in the Caribbean often reproduce colonial, Eurocentric ways of knowing and uphold global knowledge hierarchies under the guise of modernization, thus there is a need for new ways of thinking about educational barriers and system change. This article introduces the term “decolonial educational innovation,” which highlights the integration of Indigenous knowledge systems, the value of diverse epistemologies, and the support of culturally relevant, community-led pedagogies. Drawing on real examples from decolonial education efforts from the Caribbean, the article demonstrates how innovation can be understood as a relational and restorative process rather than a neoliberal goal. Ultimately, it advocates reimagining educational futures a tool to advance epistemic justice and dismantle coloniality in all its forms.

title: The Role of Teacher Empathy in Education Innovation
abstract: Research on the relationship between teacher empathy and classroom practices has yielded mixed results, potentially due to differences in measurement approach. New work that more carefully defines “adaptive teacher empathy” as a context-specific construct that combines internal and external processes, argues that this form of empathy contributes to more equitable instructional practices and improved student outcomes. The article first briefly summarizes the literature on teacher empathy, then positions adaptive teacher empathy as a driver of innovation that improves teaching and learning. The second part draws on three case examples from a project in the Eastern Caribbean to highlight how teachers applied adaptive empathy in an innovation process to develop new practices that better meet the needs of their students. Improving teacher capacity for empathy and innovation not only improves classroom practices but can be leveraged for broader system improvement through complimentary actions of school leaders and system decision-makers.

La dilution de la politique d’équité, de diversité et d’inclusion (EDI) dans le quotidien d’une faculté universitaire québécoise
abstract: Cet article analyse la construction de sens autour des plans d’action EDI dans les universités québécoises francophone, par une étude de cas dans une faculté en sciences sociales. L’analyse thématique inductive porte sur 13 entretiens semi-dirigés menés auprès de personnes professeures, à partir de l’analyse cognitive des politiques publiques et du cognitive framework de Spillane et al. (2002). Les résultats mettent en évidence une dilution de la politique EDI dû à : 1) une méconnaissance de la politique; 2) une externalisation de la mise en œuvre impliquant une perception de l’EDI comme un service rendu par l’institution; 3) une tension non résolue entre les valeurs d’excellence et de méritocratie et celles de l’EDI. Bien que les discours analysés illustrent des types d’adhésion variés à l’EDI, ils se trouvent campés dans un contexte institutionnel empêchant une construction de sens partagée autour du message de la politique.

title: How First Peoples Principles of Learning have been Included in British Columbia Offshore School Inspection Reports from 2018 to 2024
abstract: This article examines how British Columbia (BC) offshore schools integrate First Peoples Principles of Learning into the BC curriculum taught in these schools located outside Canada. BC offshore schools are in 12 countries and use the same curriculum as in BC. Students who graduate from offshore schools earn the same diploma as Canadians and often attend universities in Canada. A substantial change in the revised BC curriculum was the inclusion of Indigenous perspectives and knowledge with First Peoples Principles of Learning being one of the resources to integrate this knowledge in all courses through the curriculum. This study used content analysis and critical discourse analysis to examine text segments in 282 inspection reports published each year by the BC government. Findings indicate that BC offshore schools have shown uptake and expanded inclusion of Indigenous perspectives but mostly confined to these principles of learning as a portion of the new curriculum.

title: Letters to Bhutan: A Living Inquiry Into Bhutanese Students’ Cross-Cultural Adaptations in Canada
abstract: This study explores the lived experiences of Bhutanese international students pursuing higher education in Canada. Grounded in Gross National Happiness (GNH) as a conceptual foundation and using Karen Meyer’s living inquiry framework alongside Young Yun Kim’s cross-cultural adaptation theory, we examine how students navigate cultural transitions through four interconnected dimensions: place, language, time, and self/other. Employing creative methodology through narrative reconstruction in the form of letters to home, this research reveals complex negotiations between GNH values and Western educational paradigms. Findings suggest that students navigate complex adaptation processes across spatial, temporal, and communicative dimensions while developing intercultural identities that integrate heritage and host cultural elements through creative coping strategies. Structural factors including immigration policy, institutional support, and financial pressures significantly shape these adaptation processes. This study contributes to comparative education literature by examining an understudied population and showing how small-nation students navigate globalized higher education through s

title: Interconnections of Policies Across Territorial Borders: International Student Mobility into Canada During The COVID-19 Pandemic
abstract: In this paper, I examine the conditions that give rise to what is said in interviews with international students regarding a web of interconnected policies that regulated their mobility into Canada during the COVID-19 pandemic. I adopt Bacchi and Bonham’s (2016) post-structural interview analysis and focus on the production of two subject positions across the interviews: one that becomes associated with risk and one that becomes associated with resistance to certain policy processes. The participants in this study include master’s and PhD students from Brazil, China, Colombia, and India. My analysis suggests the need for an understanding of international student mobility in a more relational way that highlights the geopolitical aspects in the access to higher education in Canada for international students.

title: Book Review: Global University Rankings and the Politics of Knowledge

Un, le Perceptions d’enseignants à l’égard du système de codage basé sur l’approche catégorielle attribué aux élèves ayant des besoins particuliers en Alberta Perceptions d’enseignants à l’égard du système de codage basé sur l’approche catégorielle attribuée aux élèves ayant des besoins particuliers en Alberta
abstract: Le ministère de l’Éducation de l’Alberta appuie, dans ses documents officiels, l’éducation inclusive depuis plus de vingt ans (Alberta Learning, 2004). En même temps, il requiert des écoles albertaines d’avoir recours à un système de codage basé sur l’approche catégorielle ou biomédicale afin de diagnostiquer et de déterminer le choix de services offerts aux élèves ayant des besoins particuliers. Malgré le fait que cette approche soit porteuse d’une vision déficitaire de l’élève et va à l’encontre des principes fondamentaux de l’éducation inclusive, elle demeure nécessaire, voire pertinente aux yeux de plusieurs enseignants (Fortier et al., 2018). Face à ce constat déroutant, cette étude exploratoire vise à recueillir les perceptions des enseignants (n=130) provenant d’écoles francophones albertaines quant au système de codage fondé sur l’approche catégorielle attribué aux élèves ayant des besoins particuliers.

title: Book Review: Time in Education Policy Transfer: The Seven Temporalities of Global School Reform
A Tutoring Start-Up in COVID-19 Emergency: Lessons Learned
abstract: This action research study examines a university-school board virtual tutoring program developed as an emergency response during the COVID-19 pandemic to support disadvantaged students in Ontario, Canada—a distinctive and underexamined governance context within the global tutoring literature. Situating tutoring as a policy response that circulated internationally during the pandemic, the study evaluates academic and social-emotional impacts using performance data, surveys, tutor reflections, and self-assessments. Positive social-emotional outcomes and strong administrative support marked program successes, while academic gains were limited. The analysis identifies emergency program design features—including limited frequency, after-school delivery, and technical and institutional constraints—as key barriers to academic impact. The study contributes to comparative and international education research by examining how a globally circulating policy response was translated within a decentralized, risk-averse public education system, highlighting implications for equity, innovation, and university-school board partnerships. title: Book review: Resisting the Dehumanization of Refugees
“I Still Love my Country”: Supporting the Social Integration of Recent Immigrant-Origin Students Through Drawing and Philosophical Dialogue
abstract: This article explores the potential of Philosophy for Children (P4C) to support the social integration of first- and second-generation immigrant students. It presents a portion of the results of a study that took place in 2023 in a Montréal primary school. The results, based on students’ drawings, philosophical dialogues conducted with the class, and interviews with the students and their teacher, suggest that P4C activities combining drawing with group dialogue can enable immigrant-origin students to explore questions related to identity and belonging and to make connections between their experiences and those of other students. Based on these results, I propose that the Ministry of Education integrate P4C activities incorporating creative expression into the pedagogical approaches recommended for supporting the integration of recent immigrant-origin students in Quebec.

title: The Cultural Psychological Impact of Educators’ Identity on the Concept of International Mindedness in the International Baccalaureate Program
abstract: This work examines the International Baccalaureate (IB) program’s concept of international-mindedness and its application to school cultures at the International School of Prague. Its objective is to analyze the concept of international-mindedness with three different levels of identifiers (educator-self, educator-self vs. students, educator-self vs. outside school environment) to express that the nebulous and equivocal educator identity in international school(s) is veritably more complex than what is defined by the IB. Two approaches to identity in individualist and collectivist societies will be discussed to understand the identity of educators. Based on interviews with four educators at the International School of Prague, this article shows that separating “international-mindedness” from “international” can create conflicting identities among educators, particularly between individualist and collectivist self-identities, and it ultimately concludes that no sole international mind exists due to the dialectical and exclusionary nature of various international-mind identifications.

title: Book Review: Teacher acculturation: Stories of pathways to teaching
Beyond Perceived Privilege: A Case Study of a Private School’s Views on Improving Inclusive Education
abstract: Inclusive education in private schools remains an under-researched area, particularly within the Caribbean. This qualitative single-case study explores the perspectives of 27 purposively selected stakeholders—including educators, parents, students, and support staff—at a private primary school in urban Jamaica. Through thematic analysis, key barriers to effective inclusion were identified: inconsistent communication, limited staff capacity, inadequate school—community partnerships, and insufficient human and physical resources. Despite these challenges, stakeholders expressed a strong commitment to improving inclusive practices, which are examined in this article. The findings underscore the importance of grounding inclusive education policy and practice in the lived experiences of those directly involved. While not generalizable, the study offers valuable insights that can inform inclusive education efforts in both private and public schools within comparable contexts.

title: Éditorial
Editorial
In Their Own Words: Student Narratives of Intercultural Engagement, Barriers, and Impact at a Canadian University
abstract: Enhancing and evaluating intercultural learning in Canadian postsecondary education is increasingly important in the context of domestic student diversity, the rapid internationalization of higher education, and collective responsibilities to address the local and global implications of colonialism at relational, institutional, and systemic levels. This paper provides the findings of qualitative research designed to explore student perspectives on their intercultural attitudes, knowledges, and skills, as well as to identify whether and how their learning resulted in intercultural praxis. Data from a student survey coded and thematically analyzed revealed a variety of themes of interest to educators. The findings highlight the need to address individual and institutional barriers to intercultural learning, while acknowledging that societal barriers also constrict the advancement of inclusion and diversity goals. Key areas for improvement include moving beyond deficit models of cultural diversity; enhancing pedagogical supports and professional development in intercultural praxis; and progressing past superficial or individualistic approaches in ways that empower students to apply th

title: Attentes, connaissance et utilisation de styles bibliographiques d’étudiants universitaires : comparaison entre la langue, la région et les domaines d’études
abstract: Translator Les étudiants n’ont pas tous les mêmes opportunités pour apprendre à connaître et à utiliser les styles bibliographiques que ce soit en lien avec les domaines d’études, la langue d’études ou les régions où l’étudiant effectue ses études. Dans ce contexte, les résultats d'une étude comparative internationale à un questionnaire indiquent que la grande majorité des étudiants considèrent important de maîtriser les styles bibliographiques dès leur entrée à l’université. Les étudiants de certains domaines d’études sont moins formés en matière d’utilisation des styles bibliographiques et il en va de même pour les étudiants dont la langue d’études n’est pas leur langue maternelle et les étudiants de l’Europe. Ces résultats suggèrent de renforcer les mesures de soutien auprès des étudiants, notamment par une meilleure visibilité des services de la bibliothèque.

title: From Impetus to Engagement: Ecological Perspectives on Content Faculty Agency in CLIL Collaborations at a Canadian University
abstract: This qualitative case study explores the experiences of content faculty (CF) participating in interdisciplinary collaborations for Content and Language Integrated Learning (CLIL) in Canadian higher education. Using an ecological lens, this study examines the motivations, enactments, and contextual factors shaping agency across three disciplinary cases. Data from semi-structured interviews reveal that collaborative dynamics and the enactment of agency are shaped by disciplinary expertise, interpersonal relationships, and the interplay of personal histories, future aspirations, institutional structures, and professional contexts within the ecologies of these partnerships. They underscore the importance of recognizing faculty contributions and addressing institutional barriers to strengthen collaborative efforts. In addition to extending CLIL research beyond predominantly European and Asian contexts, the findings offer insights into how institutions can better support the language and literacy development of their multilingual students.

title: Recruitment and Retention of International Students in Canada During the Pandemic: An Analysis of Immigration Policy Measures
abstract: This paper examines the immigration policy measures introduced in Canada during the COVID-19 pandemic and analyzes how these measures supported the recruitment and retention of international students. The analysis spans from March 2020, when the pandemic was declared, to December 2022, when most educational institutions began transitioning back to in-person learning. Based on a comprehensive review of policy documents, the study finds federal measures that facilitated the recruitment and retention of international students, including travel regulations, online learning provisions, work-related measures, and pathways to permanent residency. Findings indicate a significant shift in policy-making from reactive to proactive strategies, emphasizing economic recovery as immediate health threats diminished. The pandemic necessitated rapid policy innovation, particularly in online learning and work-related provisions, which may influence future approaches to international education and immigration in Canada. The paper concludes with a discussion on the implications of these policies and recommendations for future research to understand their long-term effects on Canada's international educ

title: Apprendre à lire et à écrire au primaire : une étude de cas rapportant des pratiques d’enseignants à Dakar
abstract: Apprendre à lire et à écrire nécessite un enseignement explicite de connaissances et de stratégies. Or, au Sénégal, la formation des enseignants est inégale à cet égard. Dans une perspective de développement professionnel, notre équipe de recherche a mené une enquête au sujet de la formation continue en littératie. Conséquemment, une étude de cas rapportant les propos de deux enseignants œuvrant au primaire à Dakar nous a amenés à discuter des besoins de ces enseignants pour mieux guider leurs pratiques selon les composantes du modèle interconnecté du développement professionnel.

title: Éditorial
Editorial

L'équité en acte : retour sur l'expérience d'étudiant.e.s d'origine immigrante inscrit.e.s dans un dispositif novateur de formation initiale en enseignement en Alberta L’équité en acte : retour sur l’expérience d’étudiant.e.s d’origine immigrante inscrit.e.s dans un dispositif novateur de formation initiale en enseignement en Alberta
abstract: Cet article aborde l'expérience d'étudiant.e.s d'origine immigrante (ÉOI) inscrit.e.s à un nouveau cours pilote à soutenir leur insertion socioprofessionnelle en enseignement en Alberta. Ce cours a été développé et enseigné en collaboration avec deux enseignantes d'expérience d'origine immigrante exerçant dans différents contextes scolaires en Alberta. Il articule conjointement la pratique réflexive et la décentration interculturelle au moyen d’observations participante dans les écoles ainsi que les exigences d'équité, de diversité et d'inclusivité. Les données qualitatives recueillies au moyen d’un sondage volontaire auprès des étudiant.es et d’échantillon de leur travail final témoignent d’une expérience positive dans ce cours. Les ÉOI ayant particulièrement apprécié d’être confrontés au réel dans les écoles et de bénéficier de l’expertise complémentaire et ancrée de l’équipe enseignante. Enfin, la pratique réflexive et de décentration interculturelle a été un exercice novateur pour les ÉOI facilitant le passage d’un monde à l’autre, quoique plusieurs contraintes en limite son exercice.

title: Lessons Learned from a Near-Symmetrical North‒South Student Exchange/ International Service-Learning University Partnership
abstract: This article reports on an interview-based assessment of the eight-year experience of a North‒South university partnership between a Canadian university and three universities in a Sub-Saharan African country. The partnership concerned an asymmetrical student exchange program whereby southern graduate students traveled north to study while northern undergraduates traveled south to perform international service-learning internships. Unlike conventional partnerships that tend to be hierarchical and one-way, the article finds this partnership demonstrated characteristics of Koehn and Obamba’s (2014) “near symmetrical partnership” in which partners consider the relationship reasonably balanced despite acknowledging enduring power imbalances. The article identifies four factors that appear to have contributed to this near-symmetrical status: the asymmetrical nature of the student exchange program; reliance on thick ties between a small number of key actors, including a boundary spanner; deliberate efforts to counter the imbalance; and positive effects of funder regulations. The conclusion presents recommendations for funders and university partners.

title: Decolonial STEM Education and the Integration of a Critical Global Citizenship Education Framework in an Ontario Secondary School
abstract: This study explores how the HEADSUP framework can help STEM teachers integrate anti-oppressive and critical social justice frameworks into their teaching. Using a qualitative case study approach, STEM teachers and students in an Ontario secondary school participated in weekly sessions to learn about utilizing HEADSUP. Data were generated through semi-structured interviews with teachers and observations by the research team. The findings demonstrate the opportunities and challenges of decolonizing STEM education in Canadian schools through critical decolonial frameworks. Interviews with teachers revealed that integrating HEADSUP amplified students' voices and promoted active engagement in STEM classrooms. Teachers also highlighted that the HEADSUP framework helped students connect more fully with the curriculum and encouraged them to explore concepts beyond the STEM curriculum. The findings also show that utilizing anti-oppressive and social justice frameworks in STEM classrooms can be challenging due to constraints imposed by the current provincial curriculum. Implications for policy are discussed.

title: The Portrayal and Branding of British Columbia Offshore Schools on Provincial Government Websites
abstract: This article examines how British Columbia (BC) portrays its offshore school program on its government websites. BC offshore schools currently operate in 11 countries, teaching the provincial curriculum to students from the local host country. Our critical discourse analysis of BC provincial government websites and videos shows that the curriculum is portrayed as a brand and the program’s rationales and goals are inconsistent. BC portrays its curriculum as a global brand that is more progressive, modern, and worldly than the countries that host offshore schools. However recent BC curriculum initiatives, such as Indigenous perspectives and knowledge, core competencies, and place-based learning are mostly absent from the discourses on the websites and videos. Based on these findings, we propose that BC revisit the rationalization for the offshore school program and how it is officially portrayed because the portrayal of curriculum as a branded product blurs the lines between public and private spaces.

title: Temporal Trajectories: A Comparative Analysis of Mexican and Vietnamese Students’ Strategies in the Canadian Edugration System
abstract: This paper compares Mexican and Vietnamese international students’ and graduates’ migration decision-making while navigating Canadian policies merging international higher education and migration or the “edugration system.” While this system offers a delimited temporal framework and a linear pathway to permanent residency (PR) for international students; we argue that it does not align with the temporality of international students’ and graduates’ plans and aspirations. We draw from interviews conducted with 15 Mexican students and six graduates as well as 10 Vietnamese students and 11 graduates. Our findings highlight participants’ migration strategies for transnational social mobility, from childhood to postgraduation. These strategies unfold distinctively in time, depending on the region of origin. Rather than embracing the homogenizing edugration time frame, there is a need to emphasize international students’ and graduates’ own temporality to foster a nuanced and critical understanding of their migration pathways.
